seo.pirateDescription: NO Anchor University’s home port: rankings by our own parrot, a word from the Captain, life on board, research treasure, notices and events. A hackathon parody of IIT (ISM) Dhanbad.

Ranked #3 in Questionable Navigation

Knot Theory (Practical): Top 5

items.text: #1 among universities without an anchor. We checked: there is only us.
#7 among universities that float. The other six are boats.
#3 in Questionable Navigation. We were aiming for #1 and missed.
Digging: #1 in the known world. The known world is quite small.
Knot Theory, practical: top 5. The theory is still tangled.
Mechanical: top 10 for things that turn. The ship’s wheel counts.

pirate.footnote: All rankings compiled by our own parrot. It ranks us first in everything it can pronounce.

original.heading: Director’s Message
paragraphs: Welcome aboard NO Anchor University. Since 1717 we have sailed without an anchor, and we have never once regretted it. An anchor keeps a ship in one place. We would rather keep learning.

I am often asked where this university is heading. The honest answer is forward. Our students arrive with questions and leave with better ones, and somewhere along the way they learn to read a map, a balance sheet and a differential equation, usually in that order.
original.verseTranslation: (Our motto. It has served us well, wherever we are.)

pirate.heading: A Word from the Captain
pirate.kicker: Read out on deck exactly as written. Nobody edits the Captain.

items.label: Professors on deck
items.note: one for every day of the voyage

cards.text: The Film Society held its annual Silent Sea Film Festival, screening fourteen films about the ocean, none of them with sound.
Twenty-four teams competed in the annual Deck Basketball Tournament. Play was suspended twice owing to high waves.
The Crew Reunion Concert brought together current and former students for an evening of music in the Gold D. Roger Auditorium.

pirate.heading: Life on Board
pirate.tagline: Where creativity pulsates… and occasionally capsizes.

cards.text: The Silent Sea Film Festival showed fourteen ocean films with no sound. The audience was asked to provide the waves.
Twenty-four teams played in the Deck Basketball Tournament. Play stopped twice for waves and once because the ball went overboard.
The Crew Reunion Concert packed Gold D. Roger Auditorium. The building’s resident ghosts asked for an encore.

original.heading: Academics
original.tagline: Three centuries of instruction in engineering, science and management.

pirate.heading: The Learning Deck
pirate.tagline: Three hundred years of teaching. The treasure? Knowledge. Mostly.

items.title: Self-Correcting Compass
items.text: Researchers in the Department of Physics have developed a compass that recalibrates itself every six minutes, with a reported accuracy of plus or minus one ocean.

items.title: Tidal Forecasting with Machine Learning
items.text: A team from Computer Science and Engineering has trained a neural network on 300 years of ship’s logs to predict the tides. The model is correct twice a day.

items.title: Advances in Applied Knot Theory
items.text: The Department of Mathematics & Computing has classified all 1,204 knots in use on board, including 31 that cannot be untied.

items.title: Parrot Speech Recognition
items.text: Electronics Engineering researchers have presented a speech-recognition system trained on the ship’s parrots. It currently recognises nine words.

pirate.heading: Treasure Hunting
pirate.tagline: Inventiveness, imagination and curiosity for life. Sense of direction sold separately.

items.title: A Compass That Changes Its Mind
items.text: The Physics crew built a compass that recalibrates itself every six minutes. Accuracy: plus or minus one ocean. The Captain calls it the most honest instrument on board.

items.title: The Tide Predictor
items.text: Computer Science fed 300 years of ship’s logs into a neural network to predict the tides. It is right twice a day, which the crew agrees is an improvement.

items.title: Knots, Fully Classified
items.text: Maths & Computing has catalogued all 1,204 knots on board. Thirty-one cannot be untied, and one appears to be holding the ship together.

items.title: Teaching Machines to Understand Parrots
items.text: Electronics built speech recognition for the ship’s parrots. It knows nine words so far. Four of them are “cracker”.

items.title: Founders’ Day Lecture
items.text: The annual Founders’ Day Lecture addressed the theme “Purpose, Discipline and Curiosity at Sea”.

items.title: International Students’ Meet
items.text: Students from 23 countries gathered for the International Students’ Meet, hosted by the Dean (International Relations), Gold D. Roger.

items.title: Fresh Water Symposium
items.text: The Fresh Water Symposium brought researchers together to discuss the location, conservation and fair sharing of drinking water on long voyages.

items.title: Digging Week 2026
items.text: Digging Week 2026 brought students and industry together to demonstrate safer and smarter excavation techniques.

items.title: Founders’ Day Lecture
items.text: The Founders’ Day Lecture covered purpose, discipline and curiosity at sea. Attendance was excellent: the lecture hall is the only room on board with chairs.

items.title: Global Connections
items.text: Students from 23 countries met on deck with the Dean of International Relations, Gold D. Roger. Proof that some of our crew can find other countries.

items.title: Treasure Beneath Our Boots
items.text: The Fresh Water Symposium was about finding, saving and sharing drinking water on long voyages. Turns out the best buried treasure is water.

items.title: Digging Smarter
items.text: Digging Week 2026 showed off safer, smarter ways to dig. We have been digging since 1717. Now we dig with sensors.
